limits: Embedding kernel supplies the IRQ-safe lock; this is not an SMP object manager.
Handles never cross the domain boundary. No blocking VMM wait implementation is supplied.
Routing may select native, own or KernelEx implementations per export; owned bodies do not establish full NT behavior.
Owned contention yields through native Sleep(1); VMM retains Windows scheduling authority.
Owned UTF-8 conversion delegates other codepages; VEH registration is not CPU-trap/SEH integration.
Requires the existing VxD, live Supervisor and channel 2 peer; positive native Windows98-to-Kernel64 execution is unverified.
Returned handles belong to NTW32.DLL; they are not native Win32 kernel handles.
Console/process protocol has no Windows USER/GDI modern-app window/input/audio bridge.
Source inventory includes the two C dispatch APIs only, not all VxD exports or a public NT driver ABI.
CPUID signature gates VMCALL. Native negative V9 proves absent-Supervisor rejection, not positive peer execution.
Does not replace VMM scheduling or add invented VMM service ordinals.
Only software fill/blit/format conversion/linear present/map/fences are advertised.
No asynchronous GPU queue, WDDM miniport, D3D implementation or GPU acceleration is supplied.
Application-owned DIB adapter; Windows98 USER/GDI remains responsible for the window.
No replacement desktop or hardware display-driver/WDDM claim.

limits: Initializes notification/auto-reset type and signal state; does not allocate or validate an object address.

backend_apis.name: KeSetEvent
limits: Sets signal state under irq_save; boost/wait arguments are ignored by this partial provider.

backend_apis.name: KeWaitForSingleObject
limits: Nonzero waits use wait_one and its IRQL check; zero timeout polls once; mode/reason are ignored.

backend_apis.name: KeInitializeSpinLock
limits: Initializes existing driver KSPIN_LOCK; does not demonstrate SMP ownership or VMM integration.
Source binding and existing recorded component evidence only; this invocation runs no driver or Windows98 backend integration.

backend_apis.name: KeInsertQueueDpc
limits: Duplicate queued DPC returns false; source uses IRQ-saved queue mutation, not an established SMP queue.
Source binding and existing recorded component evidence only; this invocation runs no driver or Windows98 backend integration.

backend_apis.name: KeSetTimer
limits: Returns the prior Header.SignalState != 0 through timer_set, rather than the prior Header.Inserted state; no Windows98 VMM timer callback binding.
Sets Header.Inserted before admission to the bounded 32-entry timer list; a full list can leave Inserted set without scheduling that timer.
Negative due time is converted from 100 ns magnitude to milliseconds with a minimum one-tick delay; nonnegative absolute due time is approximated as one tick, not Windows absolute-time semantics.
Source binding and existing recorded component evidence only; this invocation runs no driver or Windows98 backend integration.

backend_apis.name: ExAllocatePoolWithTag
limits: Allocates actual heap bytes; this entry ignores pool type/tag; no complete NT pool/accounting semantics.
Source binding and existing recorded component evidence only; this invocation runs no driver or Windows98 backend integration.

backend_apis.name: IoCreateDevice
limits: Allocates device extension and namespace node; exclusive argument ignored; not a Windows98 device-stack registration.
Source binding and existing recorded component evidence only; this invocation runs no driver or Windows98 backend integration.

backend_apis.name: IoAllocateIrp
limits: Allocates actual IRP/stack locations; full cancellation and arbitrary driver IRP semantics remain outside this inventory.
Source binding and existing recorded component evidence only; this invocation runs no driver or Windows98 backend integration.

backend_apis.name: IofCallDriver
limits: Dispatches existing driver stack; driver callbacks use NTAPI; no Win98 IOS/PnP frontend acceptance.
Source binding and existing recorded component evidence only; this invocation runs no driver or Windows98 backend integration.

backend_apis.name: IofCompleteRequest
limits: Executes completion chain and honors STATUS_MORE_PROCESSING_REQUIRED; partial device/IRP lifetime model.
Source binding and existing recorded component evidence only; this invocation runs no driver or Windows98 backend integration.

backend_apis.name: IoQueueWorkItem
limits: All requested queue types share one worker; duplicate queue panics; caller must retain item/device lifetime.
Source binding and existing recorded component evidence only; this invocation runs no driver or Windows98 backend integration.

backend_apis.name: ExQueueWorkItem
backend_apis.irql: UP CR8/dispatcher model; normal PASSIVE system worker; allocation failure executes synchronously at caller IRQL without lowering it
limits: Normally queues through ntdrv_io.c to the existing PASSIVE system worker; allocation failure calls the callback synchronously at caller IRQL with no explicit lowering.
queue_type is ignored; this partial implementation does not guarantee deferred PASSIVE execution for every call and creates no second scheduler or object fabric.
Source binding and existing recorded component evidence only; this invocation runs no driver or Windows98 backend integration.

backend_apis.name: MmMapIoSpace
limits: Calls existing mmio_map and ntdrv_pci_note_mmio; cache argument is ignored by this partial implementation.
Source binding and existing recorded component evidence only; this invocation runs no driver or Windows98 backend integration.

backend_apis.name: PsCreateSystemThread
limits: Actual Kernel64 thread creation with NTAPI start routine; access/object attributes/process/client-id arguments ignored.
Source binding and existing recorded component evidence only; this invocation runs no driver or Windows98 backend integration.

backend_apis.name: IoGetDeviceProperty
limits: Existing bounded device-property provider; does not claim complete native Win98 PnP support.
Source binding and existing recorded component evidence only; this invocation runs no driver or Windows98 backend integration.

backend_apis.name: HalGetBusDataByOffset
limits: Supports PCI configuration bus type 4; invalid type/absent function return zero bytes, not fake success.
Source binding and existing recorded component evidence only; this invocation runs no driver or Windows98 backend integration.
